messages:
claire: opened PR to rework the 'pricing tiers & slabs' docs page — goal is to clarify slab boundaries, grace windows, and provide a Ruby + CLI example for metering checks. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/7012

ndave: Nice. Can we explicitly call out how slab billing interacts with burst credits? A one-liner rule-of-thumb would be helpful for onboarding.

priyanka: Also please avoid hard numbers for per-token prices; legal wants formulas like `cost = cost_per_unit * units`. We can include an illustrative example in comments only.

claire: plan: add a short paragraph: "Slab billing: usage is bucketed into thresholds (slabs) per billing cycle; burst credits are consumed first and do not count toward slab thresholds until exhausted." Also adding a 2-line Ruby snippet and a CLI curl example to query consumption.

dave: For the Ruby snippet, prefer showing how to pick the right slab and show a guard against eventual consistency (re-query after 60s).

priyanka: Heads-up: the Grafana panel permalink changed; include the panel UID and ask infra to confirm ACLs for hosted customers. Also add note that on-prem installs may not expose the same dashboard.

infra-bot: INFRA-1210 created to verify panel UIDs across regions and the private package deployments. Please include UID in PR.

claire: pushed changes: replaced numeric prices with variables, added a brief 'slab vs burst' callout, included a Ruby snippet and a short curl example. Also included a small FAQ entry: "Does burst usage push you into a higher slab?" Answer: "Not until burst credits are exhausted; once exhausted, subsequent usage counts toward slabs immediately."

Ruby snippet (in PR comments only):

```ruby
# conservative example: check consumption summary then decide batch size
require 'net/http'
require 'json'
uri = URI(ENV['QUOTA_ENDPOINT'] || 'https://api.redwood.inference/v1/quota')
req = Net::HTTP::Get.new(uri)
req['Authorization'] = "Bearer #{ENV['API_KEY']}"
res = Net::HTTP.start(uri.hostname, uri.port, use_ssl: true) {|http| http.request(req)}
data = JSON.parse(res.body)
remaining = data.dig('consumption','summary','normalized_remaining') || data.dig('consumption','tiers')&.map{|t| t['remaining']}&.sum || 0
# batch_size = [max_batch, remaining / avg_tokens_per_request].min
```

curl example (for support):

```
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $API_KEY" "$QUOTA_ENDPOINT" | jq '.consumption'
```

priyanka: Looks good. One suggestion: add an explicit troubleshooting line: "If slab boundaries appear inconsistent, wait 60s and re-query; if still inconsistent, open a support ticket with a snapshot of the quota response."

claire: added the troubleshooting line and included the Grafana panel UID (panel-pricing-21z) with a permalink. Tagged INFRA-1210 for ACL follow-up. Also put the illustrative numeric example in a code comment only.

docs-bot: PR opened by claire: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/7012 — reviewers requested: @dave, @priyanka. Checks queued: linkcheck, snippet-lint, spellcheck.

dave: Reviewed and left two tiny nits around wording. No blocking issues.

infra-bot: ENG-INFRA confirmed the hosted permalink and noted private installs may differ. INFRA-1210 will track making panel UIDs more consistent.

priyanka: Approved after wording tweak.

claire: Merged after CI green. Follow-ups: 1) post a short note in #release-notes, 2) open tiny SDK PR to add the Ruby parse pattern to examples, and 3) file an internal note for sales about the FAQ wording. Closing thread.
